findings.evidence: Row text: 'Every unit of work must be retried three times before it is reported as failed.' sourced to F-b1-02 with quote 'The core imports interfaces, never implementations'. The quote is verbatim, but F-b1-02 reads '1. **Every external dependency sits behind a capability interface.** The core imports interfaces, never implementations.' - design rule 1 says nothing about retries, and no record in the knowledge base states a three-retry rule. The validator also warns that this row restates F-b1-02 under agentic-stack's own quote without naming it.
findings.fix: Delete the row. If a retry policy is wanted, it belongs to compose-loop's ceiling (F-b4-02) and would have to be marked proposed.

findings.evidence: Row text: 'A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion, so every gate carries a breakage.' sourced to F-part-c-04 under the same quote build-definition-of-done and agentic-stack already carry, and the skill's own definition_of_done row cites the identical id and quote. Nothing here is gate-specific, and no owning skill is named (compose-loop's step 5 names build-definition-of-done for the same fact). The validator warns on it.
findings.fix: Delete it, or name build-definition-of-done and state the consequence specific to a gate (which gate assertion the breakage must move).

findings.evidence: Row claims 'build-ceremony already states that a ceremony number is a repository-global counter, never derived from a caller's position in its own run', sourced to T-t5-01 with quote 'Do not stop at ceremonies; run them and continue.' The quote is verbatim and is the whole of T-t5-01's text; the record states nothing about how a ceremony is numbered, so it cannot anchor the claim the row makes.
findings.fix: Cite the build-ceremony row (and its kb id) that actually fixes the global counter, or restate the row as proposed with the repository observation as its evidence.

summary: Seven composition skills, 190 rows. All 139 quotes are verbatim substrings of a cited record; two sourced rows quote a record that does not support their claim (compose-approval best_practices[4] cites design rule 1 for a three-retry rule; compose-improvement-loop best_practices[1] cites 'Do not stop at ceremonies' for a global ceremony counter). Both implement criteria were run once and pass as their expected text quotes (linked: 32 gate checks, 23/23 conformance under all-second adapters; workflow: 23 gate checks, 28/28 on both executors), and both breakage texts name an edit that exists in the harness with check names the run can print. The two dod defects are scope, not runnability: compose-agent-implement's criterion exercises none of the three agent-composition assertions it names, and compose-approval-implement's proves the executor pair rather than the two decision wires its adapters[] declares. compose-operators' expected quotes 'passed 29' where examples/end-to-end/test.sh now reports 30. Four rows restate a cap-, xc- or build- skill's claim without naming it, two are rewords of another row in the same skill.
